newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers rise, but many buyers already covered.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers rise, but many buyers already covered.

text.p: ARA bunkers rose, while the Mediterranean was steady to soft, but the bulk of buyers satisfied their requirements on Thursday, leaving nothing but a few crumbs for suppliers on Friday, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 CST was up $1/$2 a tonne to a traded range of $117/$118 by late session as barge sellers discovered thin buying of product from the bunker sector. Barges offers rose an initial $4 to an ambitious $118, but sellers were forced to withdraw to $116.
"A lot of (bunker buyers) have been worried by the volatile prices and just bought yesterday," one supplier said.
Enquiries in Rotterdam were below 10,000 tonnes.
Hamburg also rose a shade, but, unlike in the ARA market, trading improved, albeit from a poor Thursday level.
Mediterranean bunkers were steady to soft. Ports in Spain and France registered a high level of enquiries, but actual traded volumes were not remarkably high.
Fujairah bunkers hit a new high for the year, rising $2 to around $119 fob, as Singapore edged higher.
